newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent trades 16cts apart as traders play swaps.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent trades 16cts apart as traders play swaps.

text.p: Cargoes of physical Brent crude traded 16 cents apart on Monday as dealers with opposing swaps positions sought to influence the reference price, traders said.
First, Wall Street trader Phibro sold a March 1-3 cargo to Glencore, an independent trading company, for a four-cent premium over March forward paper.
Later, Phibro sold a Mar 2-4 cargo for 33 cents above April paper, equivalent to a discount of about 12 cents to March.
"This has nothing to do with the value of Dated Brent. We're in a week which is quite crucial for (Brent) CFD positions," said a trader.
Traders at Phibro and Glencore were unavailable for comment on Monday.
Elsewhere in the North Sea, Forties traded twice on Monday at a slightly softer Dated Brent +37/+38 cents a barrel. A third cargo was also sold but the price was not available.
"It's looking a touch weaker but plenty of people are unwilling to get involved until this Brent game is sorted out," said a trader.
Three Brent cargoes were due to be nominated March 11-13 loading dates on Monday, including a deferred March 9-11 from Friday.

April Brent paper shed nine cents to talk at $19.70 a barrel by 1540 GMT. The March/April intermonth spread was about five cents weaker at +43/+48 cents but April/May and May/June were broadly unchanged at +23/+27 cents and +16/+20 cents respectively.

Brent Contracts for Difference (CFDs) for this week gained about a cent to April Brent +29/+34 cents. The following week was steady at +15/+18 cents and the week after a couple of cents weaker at +5/+10 cents, dealers said.
